question: In the context of health-seeking behaviour, poverty acts primarily through a single mechanism — the inability to pay out-of-pocket costs for healthcare.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — poverty operates through multiple mechanisms simultaneously. Direct inability to pay is one pathway, but poverty also causes under-nutrition, reduces health literacy, creates time-poverty (cannot afford lost wages), and fosters mistrust of formal services. Effective interventions must address all these pathways, not just user fees.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is actually false. Poverty drives poor health-seeking through multiple interacting pathways, not just direct costs: poor nutrition reduces perceived fitness to travel; occupational insecurity discourages time off for consultations; low health literacy limits recognition of danger signs; and social marginalisation reduces trust in formal health systems.
